primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: IPEX syndrome due to FOXP3 dysfunction
mechanism: FOXP3 is a transcription factor required for the development and suppressive function of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells. Loss of FOXP3 function impairs peripheral immune tolerance, permitting widespread autoreactive lymphocyte activity and early-onset autoimmune enteropathy, endocrinopathy, and dermatitis.
vignette: A 7-month-old boy is hospitalized for persistent watery diarrhea and poor weight gain. He has severe eczematous dermatitis and was recently diagnosed with autoimmune type 1 diabetes mellitus. His maternal uncle died in infancy after a similar illness. Genetic testing identifies a hemizygous pathogenic variant in FOXP3.
lead: Which of the following immune abnormalities most directly accounts for this patient's disorder?
correct: Impaired development and suppressive function of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells, causing failure of peripheral self-tolerance
distractors: Defective AIRE-mediated deletion of autoreactive T cells in the thymic medulla, causing failure of central tolerance
Defective CD40 ligand expression on activated T cells, preventing immunoglobulin class switching in B cells
Defective NADPH oxidase activity in phagocytes, preventing generation of the respiratory burst
Defective perforin-dependent cytotoxic granule release by natural killer cells and cytotoxic T lymphocytes
distractor_notes: AIRE deficiency causes autoimmune polyendocrinopathy-candidiasis-ectodermal dystrophy through impaired thymic negative selection, not the FOXP3-associated regulatory-T-cell defect and classic infantile enteropathy/eczema/type 1 diabetes pattern.
CD40 ligand deficiency causes X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome with impaired class switching and susceptibility to opportunistic infections, rather than the severe early autoimmune triad of IPEX.
NADPH oxidase deficiency causes chronic granulomatous disease with defective killing of catalase-positive organisms and granuloma formation, not regulatory-T-cell failure.

Perforin-pathway defects can cause familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with uncontrolled immune activation, but do not produce the characteristic FOXP3-linked loss of regulatory T-cell tolerance.
key_expl: IPEX is caused by pathogenic FOXP3 variants. FOXP3 is expressed primarily in CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells and is required for their development and suppressive function. Loss of this regulatory population permits systemic autoimmunity, classically beginning in infancy with autoimmune enteropathy, eczematous dermatitis, and endocrinopathy such as type 1 diabetes.
objective: Connect FOXP3 loss in IPEX syndrome to defective regulatory T-cell function and failure of peripheral immune tolerance.
